About the Business:  A H R Mobile Pty Ltd operates a network of fast-paced retail outlets and kiosks located in shopping centres across Melbourne region. We specialize in on-the-spot mobile phone and tablet repairs, alongside selling a wide range of mobile accessories and protective gear.  About the Role:  In this dual-focused technical role, you will work directly from our retail outlets or kiosk stations, providing fast, reliable electronic repair services while assisting everyday shoppers. You will handle everything from basic component replacements to intricate logic board diagnostics and micro-soldering, while also upselling mobile accessories to store customers.  Work Structure: Full-time (38 hours per week).  Roster: Rotating roster aligned with shopping centre trading hours (including Thursday/Friday late-night trading and weekends).  Mobility: You must be flexible and willing to travel between various shopping centre locations in Melbourne region as scheduled.   Benefits   Competitive Salary: Market-aligned salary package + Superannuation (commensurate with trade experience).   Travel Allowance: Mileage/travel reimbursement provided when traveling between locations during work shifts.   Staff Discounts: Generous employee discounts on phone accessories, parts, and hardware.   Dynamic Work Environment: Engage directly with customers in vibrant, high-foot-traffic shopping centres.   Skills Development: Ongoing training in advanced micro-soldering and technical repair methods for the latest mobile device models.    Task & responsibilities   Device Diagnosis & Repair: Inspect, test, and troubleshoot faulty mobile phones, tablets, and wearable devices at the workbench using specialized diagnostic tools.   Component-Level Benchwork: Perform precise hardware repairs, including screen replacements, battery swaps, charging port repairs, speaker fixes, and micro-soldering on printed circuit boards (PCBs).   Accessory Sales & Customer Service: Greet customers, answer inquiries, and recommend/upsell mobile phone accessories (e.g., cases, screen protectors, chargers, and audio gear).   Quality Assurance: Test all repaired devices thoroughly before handing them back to the customer to ensure network and performance standards are met.   Workbench & Inventory Maintenance: Keep the workbench ESD-safe, clean, and organized, while managing stock levels for repair parts and retail accessories.   Multi-Site Coverage: Travel between designated shopping centre kiosks to cover shifts and manage repair volume during peak trading periods.    Qualification & experience   Qualifications:     AQF Certificate III in Electronics and Communications (UEE30920), Electrotechnology, or equivalent trade qualification; OR   At least 3 years of relevant hands-on trade experience in electronic equipment/mobile device repair (as per ANZSCO 342313 standards).     Technical Skills: Proven trade experience in mobile hardware diagnosis, precision hand-tool usage, micro-soldering, and PCB repair.   Customer & Sales Skills: Friendly, approachable attitude with experience in retail sales and customer service.   Flexibility & Mobility: Full availability for a rotating roster (including weekend retail hours) and a valid Driver’s License with reliable transport to move between shopping centre locations.   Communication: Excellent verbal and written English skills to interact with kiosk customers and document repair jobs clearly. Built on a foundation of integrity, speed, and personalised service, we partner with leading businesses across Australia to connect exceptional candidates with career-defining opportunities. result.description: Astern Group Pty Ltd   ASTERN GROUP PTY LTD  is seeking to employ a full-time Construction Project Manager.  You will need to work 38 hours per week. You will responsible for aiding the project staff during the construction stages of infrastructure projects The successful candidate will be responsible for the daily management, supervision, coordination, and successful delivery of civil infrastructure construction projects. This role requires strong project management skills, including contract administration, scheduling, estimating, procurement, budgeting, and stakeholder management, while ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards.                          Benefits   Competitive salary package with opportunities for career progression.   Long-term employment with a growing civil construction company.   Diverse and challenging projects   Supportive leadership team with an open-door culture.   Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.   Modern equipment, technology and systems to help you succeed.   Collaborative team environment where your contribution is valued.   Strong commitment to safety, quality and employee wellbeing.   Recognition and reward for high performance and commitment.    Task & responsibilities  The Construction Project Manager will be responsible for:   Interpreting construction drawings, specifications and contract documentation.  Planning, coordinating and managing construction projects from commencement through to completion.  Developing, implementing and monitoring project construction programs.  Procuring project materials, subcontractors, plant and equipment.  Managing project budgets and ensuring projects are completed within approved financial targets.  Monitoring project progress and ensuring milestones are achieved on schedule.  Ensuring all pre-construction requirements are completed prior to project commencement.  Managing labour resources and subcontractors to meet project objectives.  Ensuring projects are delivered in accordance with the latest approved drawings, specifications and schedules.  Coordinating the timely delivery of plant, equipment and hired materials in consultation with the Plant Manager.  Maintaining comprehensive and up-to-date project records and contract documentation.  Preparing project reports, progress claims, contract notifications and variation claims in accordance with contractual requirements.  Managing project timelines through accurate and regularly updated construction and contract programs.  Preparing and submitting updated project documentation to relevant authorities upon project completion to achieve Practical Completion (PC).  Ensuring strict compliance with company policies, and project management procedures.  Monitoring project costs and implementing corrective actions where budget variations occur.  Ensuring all variation works receive written client approval before commencement.  Liaising with engineers, consultants, clients, subcontractors, suppliers and other technical professionals.  Ensuring project personnel and contractors are appropriately qualified, experienced and perform efficiently within their assigned responsibilities.  Reviewing and approving employee timesheets and ensuring required project documentation is submitted to Payroll, Accounts Payable and Office Administration.  Promoting effective communication through Toolbox Talks, SWMS, site meetings and other project communication processes.  Ensuring compliance with all Workplace Health and Safety (WHS), Quality Assurance and Environmental Management requirements.  Promoting a positive company culture focused on safety, quality, customer satisfaction, continuous improvement and professional excellence.       Qualification & experience  The successful applicant must have:   A bachelor's degree or higher qualification in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, or a closely related discipline.  A minimum of one year of demonstrated experience as a Construction Project Manager or in a closely related role.       Experience using  Doka Formwork systems  .                            About Company    Astern Group are trained and competent to look after our environment, our workmates and ourselves, to ensure we all safely return to family and friends at the end of each working day! Job description:

 
Join an evolving recruitment team to provide high-quality, end-to-end recruitment support, working closely with hiring managers and stakeholders to deliver efficient and effective recruitment outcomes across the Department of Health.

 

 






 

The Team

Recruitment Services is implementing a new statewide operating model and structure designed to strengthen recruitment capability, improve consistency, and support a more modern end-to-end service across the Department of Health. We're building a stronger, more specialised team to support consistent end-to-end recruitment across the Department, and we're recruiting to multiple roles as part of this implementation.

Why this is a great time to join

You'll join an evolving, statewide team that is improving how recruitment works in practice - standardising workflows, lifting capability, and using technology more effectively to support managers and candidates. This is an opportunity to have real impact at scale, contribute to continuous improvement, and help attract the workforce that supports health services across Tasmania, leading to stronger Tasmanian community. 

The Role

As a Recruitment Officer, you will support the end-to-end recruitment process by:

Engaging with stakeholders with a client and customer focus, providing timely and friendly support.

Coordinating recruitment administration activities from advertising through to appointment.

Maintaining accurate and confidential records within e-Recruitment and HR systems.

Monitoring recruitment workflows and assisting the team to meet service delivery timeframes.

Responding to recruitment enquiries and providing advice through the People and Culture Portal.

Preparing and distributing recruitment and selection documentation.

Drafting applicant communications and ensuring candidates receive timely updates.

Publishing job advertisements across approved recruitment platforms.

Processing establishment changes and minor position amendments.

Supporting continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance recruitment processes and services.

Providing general administrative support to the Recruitment team as required.

You will need

Knowledge of, and-or experience within a human resources or recruitment operational environment and in the use of human resource management systems, applicant tracking systems, technical tools or databases particularly in the areas of recruitment or demonstrated capability to develop such knowledge within a reasonable timeframe.

Knowledge of, and experience in the application of recruitment practices, procedures and legislation or a demonstrated capability to develop such knowledge within a reasonable timeframe.

Well-developed interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain operational procedures and provide information to, and liaise with, clients, stakeholders and members of the public.

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Permanent full time, day worker position, working 76 hours per fortnight.

*Notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

Salary

$76,849 to $82,996 per annum. Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

Salary range is in accordance with the Health and Human Services (Tasmanian State Service) Award (HAHSA) and the Public Sector Union Wages Agreement (PSUWA).

Benefits available to eligible candidates 

A range of leave entitlements, access to additional leave incentives, generous personal leave, including family incentives, purchased leave options.

Workplace flexibility aligned our flexible work policy.

Fitness Passport - You, and your family can access 40+ fitness facilities across Tasmania for just $14.50 per week per person, or $28.05 for a family.
